reports.title: Storm headwall
reports.comment:
quick: Raining hard and 6 degrees at the highway 7am
Snowing at higher elevation with swirling winds 
Very warm even higher up

reports.title: Sunny Healy Pass
reports.comment: quick: Did a fitness skin up to Healy Pass today. Temp was -14 at the start moving to around -5 at the top. Strong inversion present during first half of day. On way up noticed large surface hoar crystals in large clearings/ avalanche run outs up to 3cm. Seemed isolated to bigger clearings around 1900-2000m. SH not present at clearing near top of pass/ tree line. Temperature appeased to be stable …

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Snow pit 300 M south of Healy Pass Trail below the ridge, east aspect, 2300 metres, 32º slope.  HS 125 cm	HSS 25 cm
CTH SP 22. 80cm on sun/wind crust 
Also had SP shear on facets; on Nov 5 rain crust at 50cm after prying with shovel.
Snowpack quite unreactive in spite of 2 prominent sliding surfaces. Storm snow powder light and dry. There was about 2 cm fresh overnight.

reports.title: Simpson paths avalanche control
reports.comment: avalanche: Avalanche control at Simpson. 12 shots and mostly no results which was very surprising as we expected results on the Dec 7 surface hoar/crust. Did get one significant size 2.5 on Simpson 1 that picked up a lot of snow in the track and ran a long distance. Lots of evidence of avalanches last 48 hours through the storm, running on Dec 7 SH and Cr.  Consider these results carefully, as the…

reports.title: 93s pit
reports.comment:
quick: Signs of instability found were one whoomf at 1500m. The next series of whoomfs with shooting cracks around 1800m.

Skied steep open trees and supported features  features, avoided over head from avy paths as there was moderate winds causing transport at tree line on the ridge. The Dec 7th is waking up and showing signs that weren't present in previous days in the area. (see Snowpack for pi…

reports.title: Floe Lake Trailhead
reports.comment:
snowpack: We digged a pit at 1345m in an opening in the new growth forest. Observed pop/drop of the Dec 7 layer: ECTP12, PST30/100, down 40 on SH 3.0-5.0.
Snow was -0.8c at ground and -2.0c at surface. Air temperature was around 0c. Minimal wind below treeline.
Trail breaking/bushwhacking was slow with the new growths. No turns were made.

reports.comment: quick: Original objective was across the highway on the SW side but about 3 or 4 other groups had the same objective at the same time and we didn’t like the idea of skiing with several other groups around, especially given some references in the avy bulletin about potential for skier triggering etc that suggested something spooky is showing up occasionally in the snowpack. reports.title: Burnt trees
reports.comment: quick: Saw an older size 2.5 or 3 on a N facing thin rocky aspect probably triggered earlier in the week from the high winds. Down lower the snow was crusty but conditions improved as we gained elevation and eventually turned to nice low density powder. Surface hoar was evident especially at the valley bottom. The slide paths were starting to get skied out but the cold temperatures faceted the tra…

reports.title: Kootenay NP NE face
reports.comment: quick: 1-5 CMS of fresh snow. No new sign of instability and snow pack is stable. minimum skidding from the new snow and no movement with a ski cut.

reports.title: White Tail
reports.comment:
quick: Lots of people out enjoying White Tail. 
20-30 of new low density snow.
Gusts and squalls throughout the day, with wind picking up in the afternoon.
Gradual warming throughout the day, -9 at the car in the morning at -1 in the evening. 
Saw some small pockets of storm snow crack and slide on the firm old surface at and below ridgetop, likely will get worse as winds continue.
New snow on ste…

reports.title: Natural large avalanches on 93s
reports.comment: quick: Witnessed two large avalanches mid-day when the sun was starting to shine and when the wind picked up. One was a small size 3 that started as a small loose slide from the ridge top, but then stepped down much deeper (old PWL?) at around 2000m. The other was a 2.5 that also started as a loose dry, but then trigged a slab in the storm snow and continued to the valley bottom. The wind was affe…

reports.title: Hawk ridge / increased hazard on solar aspects?
reports.comment: quick: After having skied a lot on the western side of the highway this winter we were surprised to find a very different snowpack on Hawk ridge. We found 30-40cm storm snow on top of a pretty faceted snowpack. This storm snow whumphed and settled wherever the sun has kissed the slope snd made the new snow into a more cohesive slab. We had 1 size 1.5 Skier remote from a few metres away on a steepe…

reports.title: Avalanche Control Results Simpson Avalanche Paths
reports.comment:
avalanche: Helicopter avalanche control on the Simpson road paths produced 10 slabs with 10 shots. 5 were size 1-1.5 and 5 were sz 2-2.5 with a depth of 40-50 cm in wind affected snow. The planned avalanche control for Mt Whymper was cancelled due to high winds and poor visibility for the second day running... we will likely revisit this Sunday or Monday as the weather improves. 
Thank you for sta…

reports.title: 93S
reports.comment: quick: Light snow but not amounting to much.  Winds were light from the E or ESE. Ski quality was great.  No signs of instability on NE or NW aspects that we skied.  Boot top ski pen when trail breaking.

reports.title: Steep EAST Release
reports.comment: avalanche: Noted a pair of releases up high on East-facing steep terrain on Serac Ridge. These are apparently old (reportedly observed Sat. Feb. 13th). Likely wind slab on leeward slope as additional wind affect visible (corniced).

reports.title: 93S NE facing slopes
reports.comment: quick: Rode a NE gully on 93S. Deep powder turns to be had. Snow is stable with minimal sluffing. Wind from the NE started as we got higher. Sign of wind loading we present on SW aspects.

reports.title: White Tail slate
reports.comment: quick: Skied around White Tail - big changes from yesterday. Lots of storm and wind slab forming in lee aspects and cornices loading. Snow was getting stripped from windward aspects

reports.title: Wardle sub peak highway path natural cornice release
reports.comment:
quick: See avalanche observation for natural cornice release obs. 

While heading up the south burns of wardle sub in the trees we received a large settlement. After quick investigation using hand shears the Jan 27th crust facet combo was propagating upon isolation. We bailed at this point.

Surface snow was crusty from likely rains upto our high point of maybe 1500m possibly higher. Had 5 to 10cm…

reports.title: Near Miss, Simpson
reports.comment: avalanche: 1st skier ski cut the line on a steeper planar area above the main part of the run, then skied about 300m down the lower angle more open part of the run into an island of safety. 2nd skier spooned turns, avalanche released above and behind him ~10m in the area that was already skied. Rest of group (4 of 6) was watching above from safe area. Initial release was described as very slow and…

reports.title: Cornice Failure
reports.comment: avalanche: Remote trigger cornice failure from above along serac ridge. Avalanche ran full time path down the 2nd gully (approx 800m) with exposed vegetation. See photos for details.

reports.title: Cornice triggered avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Cornice triggered avalanche ran down a gully feature while we were skinning up the adjacent trees.

reports.title: Avalanche south aspect
reports.comment:
incident: Avalanche trigged behind second skier on the slope.
Remote triggered second avalanche in adjacent terrain feature.
Skier on slope was able to ski to an island of safety before the avalanche caught him.
Avalanche started smaller and slow moving and stepped down got larger. The two avalanches merged at a gully (terrain trap) it got really large and fast with a big powder cloud small trees …

reports.title: Size 2 avalanche - South Ribs of Simpson
reports.comment:
incident: Size 2 triggered.
Party of three. Few loose/dry sluffs in the first turns of the day made us choose a mellower slope angle in trees. 300m into the run, following a rib, the first skier went down with no issue. The second skier decided to ski a little open pocket, bridging back into supported terrain. Turn within the pocket triggered an avalanche and propagated 60m well into the open area…

reports.title: Simpson South Aspect Fracture Line Profile
reports.comment: avalanche: Avalanche triggered by 2nd skiier on slope on Feb 27th. 2nd skiier was 5-6 turns in and slope released above them. 1st skiier was out of the way in a safe location. Nobody involved. Close call. See reporting parties MIN from Feb 27th.

reports.title: Verendrye Creek snow profile
reports.comment: quick: Snow profile on an open glade, SE aspect at 1950 meters. Objective was to locate and test the two recent PWL layers - Jan 27 and Feb 19.

reports.title: Serac - Size 2 Na persistent slab
reports.comment: quick: Size 2 natural avalanche, SE aspect, approximately 1700 m. Looks to be last 24-48 hours.
